samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because the order in which numbers are added can affect the result due to rounding errors. Different groupings of additions may lead to different intermediate sums, which, when rounded, yield different final results. This behavior is a consequence of the finite precision and the specific rounding rules used in floating-point arithmetic.
